Give a person a perk without a purchase: for a support case, a tester or compensation. They can use
it at once, alongside anything they bought, and it never counts as revenue.

It lasts --days days or --until a date, and for life when neither is given; 'voidhash person revoke'
takes it back. It is granted in production, for apps using production keys, or with --test for apps
using test keys.

Usage:
  voidhash person grant [person] [perk] [flags]

Arguments:
  person  The person's email, distinct id (the id your app identifies them by) or id
  perk    The perk's slug (what your app checks), name or id

Flags:
      --days <days>        How many days from now it lasts
  -h, --help               Show help for this command
      --json               Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --note <note>        Why it is granted, for your team, such as a ticket number; no personal
                           data
      --project <project>  Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default: this
                           directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet              Print only ids, one per line
      --test               Grant it in test, for apps using test keys, instead of production
      --until <date>       The last date it lasts, as YYYY-MM-DD (it ends at the end of that day,
                           UTC)

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash person grant ada@example.com premium --days 30 --note "Ticket 4821"
  voidhash person grant user-42 beta --until 2026-12-31 --test
  voidhash person grant person_123 premium --json
